task: Add a non-blocking startup-time readiness check for the configured model provider (Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, or LiteLLM proxy) and surface it on the existing /healthcheck endpoint.

component_scope.label: M
component_scope.affected: model_provider_readiness (new service module), main.py lifespan startup wiring, common.py /healthcheck endpoint

requirements_clarity.label: S
requirements_clarity.gaps: LiteLLM LLM_PROXY_MODE spec-compliance nuance and a missing exception guard were only caught during the review's fix-up round, not fully nailed down upfront; otherwise the provider matrix (Azure OpenAI / AWS Bedrock / LiteLLM proxy / other) was clearly specified

technical_risk.label: M
technical_risk.risk_factors: Change sits on the app startup path where an unguarded failure could block boot; boto3 local credential-chain probing (get_credentials()) used in a new context; first review pass flagged a missing exception guard and a healthcheck AttributeError fallback gap
technical_risk.mitigation: check_model_provider_readiness() call wrapped in try/except in main.py that degrades to a 'not configured' result rather than raising; healthcheck reads app.state via getattr with a None-safe fallback; module explicitly mirrors the existing oauth_security precedent's shape (pure functions, no framework, never logs secret values)

key_reasoning.reason: Three components touched (new readiness service module, main.py startup wiring, common.py healthcheck field) across Service, Bootstrap, and API layers — coordinated but each piece is small

Sits on the app-boot critical path and required a review fix-up round for a missing exception guard and a LiteLLM spec-compliance gap, but follows an established precedent module's shape and is defensively guarded end to end
